label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Tolu, first of all, I’m really sorry. I know that particular pain of checking the portal expecting one thing and seeing another. You’re not being dramatic for crying. Please don’t let anybody rush you into a decision with just “accept it” or “rewrite” without explaining what either one actually involves.

I’m literally the person you asked for. I’m in Biology 100L now, in a federal university here in Lagos, and Medicine and Surgery was what I originally wanted. I scored 251 in JAMB 2025, applied for Medicine, and was offered Biology. So I’ll tell you my own experience honestly, including the parts that are not encouraging.

The day I saw Biology on the portal, I locked myself inside my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. It wasn’t even only about the course; it was the embarrassment and having to explain to people. My mum was still telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for almost two months. I had to beg her to stop because every time somebody asked me about “my Medicine,” it felt like the thing was happening again.

So I understand why your head is scattered right now.

Now, about transfer: **it is real, but it is not automatic and it is not easy.** Kingsley saying it is a myth is not correct, at least not for my school. But favour’s “just read hard in 100L and transfer” is also too simple. Hard work is necessary, but hard work alone does not control everything.

This is what my level adviser told us about moving into MBBS after 100L in my university:

- You need a **CGPA of at least 4.50 out of 5.00**.
- Even with that CGPA, **there must be space in Medicine**. Meeting the grade does not guarantee that you will be moved.
- She said about six people were moved in from the whole faculty last year, and she thinks over 40 people applied. Those are her approximate figures, not an official list I personally saw, but it gives you an idea that many people can be chasing very few spaces.
- She also said you must have met the requirements for Medicine in **JAMB and post-UTME**, including the relevant cut-offs.

That last part is very important for you. Your 268 is a good score, but **268 alone does not establish that you are eligible for transfer**. Nobody here knows your school’s Medicine cut-off, your post-UTME score, or how your faculty combines its requirements. Please don’t let anybody use your JAMB score to promise you that transfer will work.

My own CGPA after first semester was **4.31**, not 4.50. I’m still trying, but I won’t come here and form “transfer sure” for you. That is exactly why I say people shouldn’t accept Biology with the mindset that they are only passing through it and will automatically enter Medicine.

Since you have two weeks, go to your own faculty or department as soon as possible and ask them directly. Speak to the appropriate faculty officer, admissions officer or level adviser. Ask them:

1. Does this school actually allow transfer from Biology into MBBS after 100L?
2. What CGPA is required, and is it based on the full 100L session?
3. Must I have met Medicine’s JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs for my admission year?
4. How many spaces are usually available, and how many people were transferred recently?
5. What else is required, and when does the application happen?

Try to get the exact rules for **your own school**, not general gist from forum people — including me. Rules can differ completely between universities, and they can also change. Your dad’s plan is possible in some places, but your aunty’s fear is also valid if you accept without confirming anything. Neither of them should be your only source of information.

As for Biology itself, no, it is not a bad course. I think when Medicine is the only thing you have pictured for years, any other course can initially feel like failure. That doesn’t mean the course is useless.

My 100L courses include BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Let me not lie to you, Physics and Maths are the ones dealing with many people. So when people casually say “just get 4.5,” they make it sound as if you can read Biology notes for two nights and collect it. It takes serious work.

There are also practical expenses people don’t mention when they are advising you. In my own school, my lab coat was ₦6,500 and my dissecting kit was ₦9,000. The practical manual was extra. Your own costs may be different, but just know there are things to budget for apart from accepting the admission and paying fees.

The funny thing is that my first Biology practical was part of what changed my attitude. We dissected toads, and one guy in my group actually fainted. I was fine, and somewhere during that practical I realised, “Wait, I actually like this thing.” Since then, I’ve been enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. That doesn’t mean I suddenly forgot Medicine or that everybody will have the same experience. It just means Biology has become a real course to me now, not merely a disappointing name on my portal.

That is why my honest advice is: **if you accept Biology, be prepared for the possibility of finishing with a Biology degree while you pursue transfer if you are eligible.** Don’t accept it solely because somebody has assured you that you will leave after one year. Ask yourself whether you can genuinely engage with the course if that transfer never comes.

On the other hand, rewriting is not wrong. If you consider everything and know that Medicine is truly what you want, and you are ready for another JAMB and post-UTME process without any guarantee attached, you are not a failure for choosing that route. But don’t let people romanticise staying at home either. Favour is right about that part: watching your mates resume while you are at home can affect you mentally.

One of my secondary school classmates, Ifeoma, rejected a Pharmacy offer because she wanted to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. That is her story, not a prophecy that the same thing will happen to you, but it is why “just reject it, one year is nothing” should not be said lightly. One year can become more, and there is no guaranteed Medicine admission at the end of it. At the same time, her experience is not proof that everybody who rewrites will fail.

Also, please sit with this question honestly: **do you want Medicine itself, or do you mainly want to be called “doctor” because that is what your parents and everybody around you expect?** Only you can answer that. There is no shame in wanting Medicine badly, but the decision should come from what you understand about the course and the work, not just fear of disappointing people.

So I won’t choose for you. Accepting does not guarantee transfer, and rejecting does not guarantee Medicine next year. What you can do now is get your school’s actual transfer rules before the deadline, think about your post-UTME and eligibility, and decide which risk you can live with.

Whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world. This admission letter feels like your whole future right now because the pain is fresh, but it is not the full summary of your intelligence or what your life can become. You scored 268, so please don’t let one portal update make you start seeing yourself as a failure. Breathe, ask the right questions, and make the decision with clear eyes — not while everybody is shouting different instructions at you.
